feedback: If the learner imagines the planets crowded together, have them physically traverse the gap to the next bead and count the empty metres.

If the learner shrinks the gaps much more than the sizes in their head (picturing planets close together, as in many diagrams), point out that on this model, where sizes and gaps are shrunk by the same factor, Earth is a peppercorn but sits ~26 m from the Sun — the gap is far larger than the objects.
Praise specifically when the learner names size and distance as two separate comparisons.
activities.intendedInsight: Space is mostly, staggeringly empty: the distance between planets vastly exceeds the planets' sizes. Size and distance are two different comparisons; when both are shrunk by the same factor, as in this model, the gaps turn out to be enormous compared with the objects, unlike diagrams that squeeze the gaps to fit planets on a page.
learnerActions: Lay out (physically, with real objects, or by scrolling across a model) the Sun as a football and the planets as tiny beads at their true relative distances.
Scroll or walk across the empty gaps to reach each planet; find Earth as a lone peppercorn roughly 26 metres (an approximate anchor) from the football-sized Sun.
Say in your own words two separate things: how tiny the planets are compared with the Sun, AND how enormous the empty space between them is.
Predict before you look: are the planets crowded close together, or far apart? Then check against the model.
activities.title: Scale model: size versus distance

feedback: If a free flight disorients the learner about which layer they are in, return to the breadcrumb tether and name the current layer before moving on.
Ask the learner to re-state the nesting order after the flight to check the layer structure survived the motion.
activities.intendedInsight: Cosmic structure has genuine depth; flying outward can convey the three-dimensional arrangement of the nested layers and reinforce how small each level is within the next.
learnerActions: Take a guided flight outward from Earth while layer labels appear: solar system → galaxy → local group → cosmic web.
Keep a tether or breadcrumb back to Earth in view, and point to 'we are here' as each new layer appears.
After the flight, say which layer contains which, from smallest to biggest.
activities.title: Guided flight outward (depth view)
